summary:
EARTH PULSE - Listen to Climate Data

We are Nova Team from Egypt. Our project is EARTH PULSE, a website that lets anyone hear climate change, not just see it in a graph. Our slogan is: Don't just read climate change. Listen to it.

The problem is that students find climate graphs boring and hard to understand. Numbers like +1.28°C feel abstract and far away. Climate data is not accessible for people who learn better by listening or who struggle with graphs.

Our solution is sonification, turning numbers into sound. Every year from 1880 to 2025 has a sound. When temperature is low, the sound is low, slow, and calm. When temperature is high, the sound is high, fast, and urgent. When you press "Listen to Earth's Pulse", you hear 146 years in 60 seconds. You can hear the Earth getting hotter.

We used real NASA GISTEMP v4 data from NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies. In 1880, the anomaly was -0.18°C. In 2024, it was +1.28°C, the hottest year ever recorded. Source: https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp

Our website has a Listen button, an interactive graph, a quiz with missions, and Earth Buddy, a friendly guide for children. It is built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Audio API, and http://Chart.js.

Live Demo: https://magnificent-stroopwafel-f262e0.netlify.app

Team: Rodina - Founder & Lead Developer, Nadine - Data Assistant, Karen - Research Assistant. Climate change is not just numbers. It is the pulse of our planet. With EARTH PULSE, we give the Earth a voice.
details:
EARTH PULSE — Listen to Earth's Heartbeat
Created entirely by Rodina, a 15-year-old solo developer from Egypt.

1. How it works & Benefits:
EARTH PULSE is an interactive web platform that uses a technique called "Sonification" to transform raw NASA climate data into immersive sounds and visuals. Instead of reading complex charts, users can "hear" the climate. For example, as the global temperature anomaly increases (using real NASA GISTEMP data), the pitch and speed of the sound increase, creating a sense of urgency. This makes complex data accessible and understandable for everyone, including children and visually impaired individuals. It provides educators with a novel tool and allows anyone to emotionally connect with the planet's health.

2. Tools and Technologies Used:

· Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (built from scratch with no heavy frameworks to ensure high performance).
· APIs: Web Audio API (to generate the climate sounds/oscillators), Canvas API (for real-time data visualization), and Fetch API (to pull live data from NASA's official servers).
· Data Source: Real, verified data from NASA GISTEMP (1880–2025).

3. Creative Aspect & Innovation:
The core innovation is turning invisible scientific numbers into an emotional, audible "heartbeat." I also created a custom "Judge Mode", a 60-second automated tour that guides the judges through the app's features seamlessly. Furthermore, the platform includes "Earth Buddy," a pre-programmed AI educational assistant that explains climate concepts simply to users.

4. Factors Taken into Consideration:

· Accessibility (WCAG Standards): I added a text-resizing toggle (A+), high-contrast colors, and ARIA labels to ensure the platform is inclusive for people with disabilities.
· Scientific Integrity: I strictly used complete data up to 2025 and explicitly labeled the sea-level rise scenarios as illustrative models to maintain scientific transparency.
· Global Reach: I built a multilingual system (Arabic and English) to ensure the message reaches a global audience.
